images.caption: Codex Alexandrinus: the text runs on past 16:8 into verses 9 to 20.
Codex Washingtonianus: Mark 16:12-17, the long ending, with a saying after 16:14 found in no other Greek manuscript (the “Freer Logion”).
images.author: Unknown author

images.caption: Codex Sinaiticus: the Lord’s Prayer ends “but deliver us from evil”, with no “for thine is the kingdom”.
images.author: Unknown author

images.caption: Codex Sinaiticus, 1 John 5:7-8: “there are three that testify, the Spirit and the water and the blood”, with nothing of the Father, the Word and the Holy Ghost.
images.author: Pvasiliadis

images.caption: Codex Sinaiticus: John 7:52 runs straight on to 8:12, with no story of the woman between.
images.author: Alastair Haines

archive.credit: Codex Bezae Cantabrigiensis, photographic facsimile (Cambridge University Press, 1899)

images.caption: Codex Bezae, folio 133b: John 7:43 to 8:4. After 7:52 the text runs on, “and each went to his own house, but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives”, into the story of the woman.
images.author: Codex Bezae Cantabrigiensis, photographic facsimile (Cambridge University Press, 1899)

archive.credit: Facsimile of the Washington Manuscript of the Four Gospels in the Freer Collection, ed. Henry A. Sanders (University of Michigan, 1912)

images.caption: Codex Washingtonianus: John 7:46 to 8:16. “Out of Galilee arises no prophet” (7:52) runs straight into “Again Jesus spoke to them” (8:12).
images.author: Facsimile of the Washington Manuscript of the Four Gospels in the Freer Collection, ed. Henry A. Sanders (University of Michigan, 1912)
